note: Append-only (GDD 1.4). One entry per line. Status is failing or passing; the runner promotes with --promote and never demotes.

tests.passes_when: All JSON validates; every referenced id and line id exists.
boot.tscn launched headless runs 600 frames at a fixed 60 fps and exits 0 with no error output; the five autoloads exist and every data file loads and validates.
Travel time from G to every anchor matches section 16.2 within 0.02 s.
Hand speed left of the hub is 70% of normal.

Pointer and hand rules of 4.2 and 4.7: the pointer snaps to the nearest anchor within anchor_snap_radius and to none beyond it; with no anchor in range the hand targets the point under the pointer on the plane in front of the eye; a press made up to input_buffer before the hand arrives is applied on arrival and an older press is not; holding grip with the pointer on the wheel makes the hand fly there and grip; the glance turns the camera by glance_gain of the excess over glance_start, capped at glance_max_yaw and glance_max_pitch.
Released at 135 degrees, the wheel reaches centre in 0.675 s.

Wheel rules of 4.3: the hand grips only within grip_zone_half_width of the rim and takes the wheel at whatever angle it has, without snapping it; while gripped, pointer motion turns the commanded angle by steer_deg_per_px per pixel at 1080p, scaled by window height and the sensitivity setting, and clamped to plus or minus wheel_max_angle; the wheel follows the commanded angle with wheel_smoothing as a first-order lag.
Scripted lever paths engage gears 1 to 4, and 5 only with Fifth gear.
A release mid-channel and a push into a wall each produce one grind.

Each gesture primitive of 4.4 is recognised from scripted input and its failure case is rejected: TAP (release within 0.25 s; a longer press is not a TAP), HOLD(t) (an early release cancels with no effect), FLICK(dir) (at least 40 px within 0.25 s, in each of four directions), DRAG_TO (press on the object, release on another anchor), CRANK(n) (cumulative angle in one direction for n full turns), BEAD (repeated TAPs, at most 3 per second).
From lane centre, straight, gear 3, hands off: the car edge reaches the lane line at 3.4 s, within 0.05 s.
Full lock at 100 km/h settles at 5.0 m/s sideways.
2,500 m takes 90.0 s in gear 3 and 69.2 s in gear 4, within 0.5 s.
Braking from 100 km/h to rest takes 3.33 s.

Speed and road-edge rules of 4.8, 5.1 and 5.4: after the brake is released the car climbs to the gear's cruise speed at accel; after a downshift it slows at engine_brake; in neutral it coasts down at neutral_coast; the rough shoulder caps speed at shoulder_speed_cap; touching a guardrail or barrier is a scrape and pushes the car hit_pushback back; curve drift is k times (speed/100) squared, outward, capped at curve_cap; a gust pushes gust_push for gust_duration.
A closing speed of 20 km/h gives a scrape: 1 lamp, +10 Nerves, speed drops 20%; the car is pushed hit_pushback clear and cannot be hit again for hit_immunity.
A closing speed of 50 km/h gives a crash: 2 lamps, +20 Nerves, forced into first gear.
A closing speed of 90 km/h, or any oncoming vehicle, gives a head-on: 3 lamps, +30 Nerves, forced into first gear.

Close calls of 5.7: passing a vehicle with under close_call_gap of sideways gap and at least close_call_min_closing of closing speed, without contact, is one close call, judged when the two stop overlapping along the road; it pays close_call_base_cash times the gear multiplier, double when oncoming, and adds 2 Nerves; a wider gap, a slower closing speed or a contact is not a close call.
Chained close calls multiply by 1.25 steps and cap at 3.
Each threshold switches its impairment on and off; a Snap resets Nerves to 70.
Below the floor and not Awake: a blink of 0.3 s every 6 s with a tell 1 s before.
Every Awake source suppresses Lids, Blink and Nod for its duration.

Nod and ambient rates of 5.8 and 6.1: at nod_depth or more below the floor and not Awake the eyes shut for nod_length every nod_period with a tell nod_tell before, and the rumble strip or any hit ends the Nod and adds 15 Nerves; each vehicle within traffic_radius adds traffic_rate per second, capped at traffic_rate_cap; an empty road (no vehicle within empty_road_radius and no encounter) changes Nerves by empty_road_rate; the heavy floor follows the act as heavy_floor states.
The fifth lamp is a Wreck; capacity changes apply.

Faults of 6.3: each hit draws as many faults as it lights lamps from the Telling's fault deck, a seeded shuffle (same seed, same order); each of the seven faults applies its listed effect; a repair removes the chosen fault and its lamp.

The base cabin of 4.6, 6.2 and 7.4 works as specified: horn (cars and taxis within 40 m ahead in his lane move over, trucks and buses ignore it, -3 Nerves at most once per 10 s), wipers (one sweep keeps rain clear for 6 s), radio (station effects of 6.2; the signal drifts to static after 40 s), cigarettes (light, 25 s burn, ash once mid-burn, craving, haze), tea (3 sips; hot -12 and Awake 40 s; cold after 40 s -3), visor photo (-20 once per leg; down 3 s), slap (+12 and Awake 20 s) and window (CRANK(3); Awake 30 s; open-window effects).
For 500 seeds and all nine leg types, every rule in section 9.2 holds.
The same seed gives a byte-identical leg.

Act rules of 9.1, 9.4 and 12.3 hold in generated Tellings: leg types come only from the act's pool; a leg carries a modifier only from Act 2, only one it allows, on about one leg in three in Act 2 and two in three in Act 3; late signallers appear only from Act 2 (15% then 30%); traffic density is the leg's base plus 2 per act after the first.
Each row of section 6.5 changes Suspicion by its amount.
Open road: 3 lanes, light traffic and long empty stretches (CALM beats may be adjacent); par 90 s.
Rush: heavy traffic with frequent merges; par 90 s.
Rain: the view blurs over 6 s without a wiper sweep and sideways response is 30% slower; par 95 s.
Night blackout: the road is unlit, the view is the headlight cone (60 m, 100 m on high beam) and hazards appear late; par 90 s.
Roadworks: three 150 m chicanes one lane wide (2.16 m) between cones; par 100 s.

Tailgater: a driver sits on the bumper for 40 s, adds 1 Nerves per second and rams (a scrape from behind) if the player brakes; he leaves when the player changes lane and holds it for 3 s, then passes and brakes hard in front once; fourth gear for 10 s also loses him.

Patrol: a police car follows for patrol_duration; blue lights show in the mirror 3 s before Suspicion starts, about 20 s into the leg; at 100 Suspicion he is pulled over and pays by licence (fine) or banknotes (bribe) as 6.5 states.
Two-lane: an undivided road; trucks ahead hold 60 km/h; oncoming vehicles arrive every 6 to 10 s; each gap is long enough to pass one truck in gear 4; par 100 s.

Motorcade: five black cars hold all lanes at 70 km/h; within 100 m a spotlight gives Glare 80% and +2 Nerves per second; the motorcade never touches him; staying behind for the whole leg takes 129 s; one side road mid-leg is a Two-lane detour that rejoins ahead of the motorcade; par 110 s.

A Telling follows 11.1: Fork, Leg, Exit and Stop three times, then Boss and Boss stop, for three acts, then Arrival; the fork branch is decided by which side of the gore point the car is on; there is no fork after an act's third leg; an Exit needs the slip lane and exit_max_speed or less at 2,330 m, and a missed Exit adds 5 Nerves.
Wreck and restart: when every lamp is lit the Telling ends in a Wreck; the Telling restarts from Baghdad with the starting cabin, wheel in hand within wreck_to_wheel.
90 real seconds of driving is 30 game minutes.

Stops of 9.6: each stop charges its Clock minutes on entry and offers its service; a TAP on an offer buys it when cash allows (cash never goes below 0) and a DRAG_TO places it in a slot; gripping the wheel for 0.5 s leaves; the shady guy joins the next stop only after a leg with no lamp lit and adds 5 minutes when used; after a boss the player takes one free item out of 3 and one service at no Clock cost; shop rarity follows rarity_by_act.

The save file of 13.7 round-trips: a save made at a stop or after a boss, loaded again, restores table, seed, act, leg, clock, cash, Nerves, faults, items, adaptations, passenger, fault deck and RNG state exactly, and the Telling continued from it matches the uninterrupted one; nothing is written during a leg.
A recorded input log replays to the same final state hash.

Cigarettes (7.4): HOLD 1.2 s lights one from a pack of 10; lit for 25 s gives no Tremor, Awake and -10 Nerves over the burn; Haze +2% per second while lit, clearing 3% per second after; it must be ashed once mid-burn (FLICK) or ash falls (+5 Nerves); Craving +8 Nerves once if another is not lit within 30 s; restock 15.

Tea glass (7.4): HOLD 0.6 s sips; 3 sips; a hot sip is -12 Nerves and Awake 40 s; cold after 40 s, a cold sip is -3 Nerves and no Awake; it spills in a crash; refill 2 cash at a fuel station, free at a tea stall.
Worry beads (7.4): at the mirror, each BEAD tap is -2 Nerves, at most 3 per second; no supply; price 30.
Sunflower seeds (7.4): TAP 0.3 s starts 20 s of chewing: Awake, and immune to Nerves from honks, tailgaters and Doubts; 12 handfuls, restock 5; price 10.

Phone (7.4): a call every 25 to 40 s; three TAPs within 5 s of the first ring answer it, eyes-down; a dispatcher call pays 10 cash; one call in four is Um Noor: -8 Nerves; a missed call is +4 Nerves; using it in a Patrol is +30 Suspicion; price 35.

Energy drink (7.4): HOLD 0.6 s; Focus for 30 s (the road runs at 85% speed while the hand runs at full speed) and Awake 60 s; +10 Nerves at once, then Tremor amplitude +50% for 20 s; 3 cans, restock 10; price 30.

Painkillers (7.4): HOLD 1.2 s at the face; Tremor halved for 60 s and the Phantom muted for the leg; Heavy floor +15 for the rest of the leg; the hand at his face blocks the lower-centre view; 6 pills, restock 15; price 40.
Mixtape (7.4): music that never drifts, -1 Nerves per second; it must be flipped every 60 s (DRAG out and in, 0.8 s) or it warbles, +0.5 Nerves per second; price 25.
Tissue box (7.4): one wipe (DRAG across the glass, 0.8 s) clears all Haze; 6 tissues, restock 5; price 15.
Breath mints (7.4): TAP 0.3 s; police ignore Courage for 60 s; 5 mints, restock 5; price 15.

Arak flask (7.4, contraband): HOLD 0.7 s sips; each sip is -5 Nerves and one Courage stack, up to 3, 45 s each; per stack +50% close-call cash and -30% Nerves gains, with Sway and 40 ms of Lag; 6 sips, restock 20; sold only as a Deal for 45.
Seven-eyed charm (7.5): the first scrape each leg lights no lamp; it hangs at the mirror; price 40.
Air freshener (7.5): Haze clears twice as fast; it hangs at the mirror; price 25.
Thermos (7.5): on the seat; Far reach and HOLD 1.0 s refills the tea, hot, on the road; 4 refills; price 30.
Duct tape (7.5): the first fault each act repairs itself after 10 s; price 35.
Lucky note (7.5): +1 cash per close call; price 35.
Cracked sunglasses (7.5): Glare -70%; night legs 15% darker; price 25.
Taxi sign (7.5): on the roof; calls pay 5 more and come twice as often; price 40.
Crossover stalk (7.6): the indicator moves to the right of the column, reach 0.10 s instead of 0.41 s; takes a bay; price 40.
Console window switch (7.6): the window opens with HOLD 0.6 s at a Near anchor instead of a cross-reach and three turns; takes a bay; price 35.
Spinner knob (7.6): the wheel turns 40% faster per pixel; self-centring is halved; takes a bay; price 50.

Wheel ring (7.6): the hook hangs at the wheel; setting it (TAP, 0.3 s) locks the wheel at its current angle for up to 4 s, then a 6 s cooldown; it locks the angle, not the lane, so drift still applies; takes a bay; price 60.
Thumb keypad (7.6): horn and wipers work while gripping, by middle click and scroll; takes a bay; price 55.
Fifth gear (7.6): unlocks gear 5 in the gate (160 km/h, close-call cash x3); takes a bay; price 60.
Loud horn (7.6): every vehicle yields and the horn gives -5 Nerves; +15 extra Suspicion per honk; takes a bay; price 45.
Bull bar (7.6): lamp capacity +1; sideways speed -15%; takes a bay; price 55.
Fog lamps (7.6): visibility +40% in rain, dust and night; oncoming drivers flash back, +2 Nerves each; takes a bay; price 40.
Wide mirror (7.6): mirror tells arrive 5 s earlier; the mirror covers more of the windscreen; takes a bay; price 35.
Forged papers (7.7): passes the next checkpoint's Papers phase automatically; 60 cash; contraband until used.
Tinted glass (7.7): Suspicion gains halved; lamp capacity -1; night legs 20% darker.
Turbo (7.7): gears 4 and 5 gain 15 km/h and close-call cash is x1.5; lamp capacity -1; braking 30% weaker.
The good stuff (7.7): the Courage cap rises to 5; 30 cash; 40 ms of permanent Lag.
Tea + Cigarettes (7.8): a sip while lit makes that cigarette burn 10 s longer.
Cigarettes + Air freshener (7.8): no Haze from smoke.
Beads + music, radio or tape (7.8): each bead is -4 Nerves.
Flask + Photo (7.8): looking at the photo with Courage gives -40 Nerves, and all stacks are lost.
Flask + Painkillers (7.8): Lag doubles and close-call cash doubles.
Wheel ring + Spinner knob (7.8): on straights the hook holds the lane centre instead of a fixed angle.
Phone + Taxi sign (7.8): three calls answered in a row pay a 20 cash bonus.
Seeds + Tea (7.8): the tea does not go cold while he chews.
Crossover stalk + Thumb keypad (7.8): he indicates automatically when a lane change begins.

The Phantom of 7.9: a cross-reach begun at Nerves 60 or more, or while Lids are active, leaves 0.25 s late with a ghost left hand as the tell; the weather cramp fires once per Rain leg, Night leg and Storm at a fixed point: after a 1.5 s hum the hand can neither let go nor take hold for 0.5 s, and +10 Nerves; painkillers counter both, an adaptation that removes a cross-reach removes its flinch, and the setting turns both off.

The Checkpoint of 10.2: a stop-and-go queue in first gear between barriers 2.34 m apart, where touching a barrier is a scrape and +25 Suspicion; Stow, 10 s, where each contraband item left out is +40 and each Courage stack +15; Papers, where the signed document is found, the window is cranked open and the document is dragged to the driver's window, with +10 Suspicion per 5 s of delay; under 50 he passes, from 50 to 99 he is searched (15 game minutes, contraband taken), at 100 he is turned back (30 game minutes and the queue again); 60 cash through the window passes at any level; modifiers Long queue and Thorough.

The Storm of 10.3: 2,000 m measured by distance, so stopping never shortens it; visibility alternates 12 s thick (15 m) and 8 s thin (40 m); gusts push at 2 m/s, each announced 1 s ahead; each wiper sweep adds 10% Haze and an open window adds 5% per second; stopped on the shoulder with hazard lights on is always safe, without them a rear-end crash is risked every 10 s; the weather cramp fires once; modifiers Crosswind and Night storm.

Dawn and Arrival of 10.4 and 10.5: false dawn, an orange glow on the right while rush traffic builds; sunrise ahead and to the left with Glare 60%, blocked for 3 s by flipping the visor; a last checkpoint passed at 70 km/h between barriers; the Call starts 833 m from the end and rings for 8 s; Arrival: he brakes to a stop in the marked bay and a TAP on the key reads the Clock; modifiers Market day and Early sun.
All four responses to the Call resolve as section 10.4 states.

The Hajjiya (8.2): on a tap she holds the wheel dead straight for up to 6 s; smoking or the flask adds 10 Nerves; in gear 4 or above she prays aloud, +3 Nerves per second; she rides 3 legs; on leaving, food once (-20 Nerves) and the first scrape after she leaves lights no lamp. She takes the seat and boards by a Far reach TAP on the passenger door (8.1).

The Conscript (8.2): his uniform halves all Suspicion gains; he sleeps and his snoring lowers Nerves by 0.5 per second; a tap or the horn wakes him for 20 s, and only then does a tap make him light a cigarette and hand it over with no ritual time; he rides to the end of the act; fare 10.

The Drummer (8.2): while he drums, the music effect without the radio, and Awake; a tap toggles the drumming; on a tap he passes the tea so sipping becomes an at-wheel reach; his drum blocks the right 10% of the view; drumming during a Patrol adds 10 Suspicion per second; he rides to Basra and pays nothing.

The Student (8.2): she answers every call for him (the cash without the hand); fork signs show 5 s earlier; she talks: Awake; each scrape adds 5 Nerves; gear 4 in rain adds 2 Nerves per second; she rides 3 legs; fare 20.

The Apprentice (8.2): he repairs one fault per leg, leaning across the gear lever for 3 s, announced 2 s ahead, during which no shift is possible; on a tap he holds the wheel at its current angle for 3 s; he retunes the radio to static every 30 s; he rides to Basra and pays nothing.
The Children (11.2): one free rewind, the first Wreck returns to the start of that leg; prices -25%; heckles are Twists and the Fib; unlocked from the start.
The Drivers (11.2): base rules; heckles are Dares; unlocked by winning the Children's Table on time.
The Uncles (11.2): a Patrol leg in every act; Checkpoint Suspicion gains x1.25; heckles are Doubts; unlocked by winning the Drivers' Table on time.
The In-laws (11.2): no contraband, no Deals, no bribes; each Snap costs 15 game minutes; heckles are Questions; unlocked by winning the Uncles' Table on time.
The Aunts (11.2): Heavy floor +10 all night; prices +25%; he starts with a Thermos and seeds; heckles are Orders; unlocked by winning the In-laws' Table on time.
The Groom (11.2): he leaves at 22:45; any boss begun without a passenger starts with +20 Nerves; heckles are Dares, Doubts and Orders; unlocked by winning the Aunts' Table on time.

Noor (11.2): one fixed road with no forks, in the order Open road, Rush, Rain, Checkpoint; Night blackout, Patrol, Roadworks, Storm; Tailgater, Two-lane, Motorcade, Dawn; the starting cabin plus beads and a full pack; no shops but tea and repairs; no heckles; the Student waits at the second stop of Act 2; unlocked by winning the Groom's Table on time.

Heckles of 11.3: one per leg in Act 1 and two per leg after, never during an encounter or a boss; the subtitle appears heckle_lead before anything changes; each type resolves as its row states: Twist, Dare, Doubt, Question, Order and the Fib.

Endings and persistence of 11.4 and 11.5: a Wreck restarts the Telling; parking after 06:00 is Late and unlocks nothing; parking by 06:00 unlocks the next Table; answering the Call and parking by 06:00 marks the Table told true and, at Noor's Table, starts the finale; passengers carried to Basra become wedding guests who add two heckles to the pool; the first win unlocks Commute mode and any Call ending unlocks Endless Night mode.

The prologue of 10.1: it plays on first launch and can be replayed from the title; it lasts 75 s and cannot be failed; its seven steps run in order with the left hand holding the lane, so no reach has a cost; it then cuts to tonight at 22:00, rolling in first gear with the wheel unheld, and the narrator says narrator.start.
The finale ends only when the grip input is released; it runs 5 simulated minutes without ending otherwise.
Every menu and every in-game action is reachable with pointer motion and two buttons.
Every setting of 17.1 exists with its options and default, is saved and loaded, can be changed mid-Telling, and has its stated effect.
Every scene (boot, title, wedding, and drive in each of its DriveContext kinds) launched headless runs 600 frames at a fixed 60 fps and exits 0 with no error output.
The balance runner completes and writes its report. It reports against section 12.5 and does not fail on the numbers.
A scripted ideal driver in gear 3 clears every generated leg with no contact.

Touch of 4.1 and 17.4: the right thumb is the hand and lifting it lets go; TAP rituals perform automatically when the hand arrives while HOLD, DRAG and CRANK need the gesture; the brake is a pedal zone at the bottom left; tap targets are at least 9 mm across; export presets exist for Windows, Linux, macOS and iOS.
